title: First-Step Speed
intro: Twenty-five minutes on the first two steps. Ten of that is the warm-up, and that is not padding — you cannot sprint off a cold hip.
Full rest between every effort. This is a speed session, so quality is the whole point; the moment you shorten the rest it becomes conditioning and stops training speed.

before.label: Not today
before.text: A sore ankle, knee, calf, hamstring, groin or Achilles, or an injury in the last month? Get it looked at first.

before.label: Stop and get it checked
before.text: A sharp pain, pain that spreads, numbness, swelling, a joint that gives way, or a sudden pull or pop.

before.label: Stop now
before.text: Chest pain, dizziness, a heartbeat that races or skips, or breathing that doesn't feel right. Get it looked at before you train again. Told to be careful with hard exercise? Check with your doctor first.

before.label: Past injury
before.text: Ever torn a hamstring, or coming back from a knee or ankle injury? Ask whoever treated you if sprinting is OK.

before.label: Check the space
before.text: About twenty-five metres of flat, non-slip ground, and court shoes. Mark each distance with tape or a line, not cones or bags you could step on.

before.label: Keep clear
before.text: 48 hours away from another hard session, and not the day before a match.

before.label: First time
before.text: Do three split-step sprints instead of six, and two falling starts instead of four.

good: Easy pace until you are warm and breathing
Nothing here is fast yet
bad: Starting hard — you are about to sprint

good: Hold the fence, stand tall, let the leg swing freely
Build the range across the ten
bad: Arching the back to throw the leg higher

good: Step wide and sit into that hip, chest tall
Feel the inside of the straight leg
Drive the back hip down, then rotate and reach tall
Feel the front of the back hip open
bad: Rotating before the hip has opened

good: Tall hips, strike the ground underneath you
Rhythm first, height second
bad: Reaching the foot out in front of the body

good: Stiff ankles, off the ground as fast as you land
Quiet contacts
bad: Bending the knees and turning it into a squat jump

exercises.name: Build-Up Run

good: Accelerate smoothly to the top speed of each one
The last one should feel fast but relaxed
bad: Going straight to full effort on the first one

exercises.note: This is the bridge between warm and sprinting — do not skip it.

exercises.name: Split-Step to Sprint

good: Land the split-step already loaded, then explode into the first stride
Stay low for the first two steps

exercises.note: Full rest between every one — this is a speed session, not conditioning.

good: Lean from the ankles until you have to catch yourself, then run
Let the first three steps be long and low
bad: Bending at the hips instead of leaning from the ankle

good: Split-step on the baseline, then one hard push-off and set
The first step goes where you are going, not across your body
bad: Landing the split-step flat and heavy

good: From the tramline, shuffle back to the middle and set
Stay low the whole way, facing the net
Drop-step back three steps, then turn and drive forward
Open the hip to turn
bad: Turning your back on the court
